8.1.1.v: From here up to यथास्वे यथायथम् [[8.1.15]], inclusive, is to be supplied always the phrase 'the whole word is repeated'.
8.1.1.e: In the contexts that will henceforth be told till the sutra > [[8.1.16]], the participating words will get duplicated.
8.1.1.sa: इतः परम् > [[8.1.16]] अस्मात् प्राक् यद् किमपि वक्ष्यते, तत् सर्वम् द्विरुक्तम् भवति ।
8.1.1.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

8.1.2.v: Of that which is twice uttered, the latter form is called अम्रेडित (repeated).
8.1.2.e: When a word gets replicated in the 'सर्वस्य द्वे' अधिकार, the second occurrence is known as आम्रेडित.
8.1.2.sa: > [[8.1.1]] अस्मिन् अधिकारे द्वित्वे कृते, द्विरुक्तस्य यत् द्वितीयम् तस्य आम्रेडितम् इति संज्ञा भवति ।
8.1.2.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

8.1.3.v: That which is called अम्रेडित (repeated) is gravely accented.

8.1.4.v: The whole word is अम्रेडित (repeated) when the sense is of 'always' and 'each'.

8.1.5.v: The word परि is repeated when used in the sense of 'with the exception or exclusion of''.

8.1.6.v: 1. प्र 2. सम् 3. उ and 4. उत् are repeated when by so doubling, the foot of a verse is completed.

8.1.7.v: 1. उपरि 2. अधि and 3. अधस् are repeated when it expresses uninterrupted nearness.

8.1.8.v: A Vocative, at the beginning of a sentence, is repeated, when envy, praise, anger, blame, or threat is meant by the speaker.

8.1.9.v: When एक is repeated, it is treated like a member of a बहुव्रीहि समास ।

8.1.10.v: A word is repeated and is treated like a member of a बहुव्रीहि समास when a mental distress over something is expressed.

8.1.11.v: In the following rules, the double-word is treated like a कर्मधारय समास ।

8.1.12.v: An adjective is repeated, when it is meant to express that the said attribute belongs to a thing only to a limited degree and the double word is treated like a कर्मधारय समास ।

8.1.13.v: The words प्रिय and सुख are repeated optionally when they mean 'easily, without any difficulty'.

8.1.14.v: The word यथायथम् is irregularly formed in the sense of 'respectively, fitly, properly'.

8.1.15.v: The word द्वन्द्वम् is irregularly formed in the sense of 'secret' and when it expresses a 'limit', 'a separation', 'employing in a sacrificial vessel' and 'manifestation'.

8.1.16.v: Up to इडाया वा [[8.3.54]], inclusive, should be always supplied in every subsequent sūtra the phrase 'of a word' or 'to the whole of a word'.

8.1.17.v: Up to सगतिरपि तिङ् [[8.1.68]], inclusive, should always be supplied the phrase 'after a पद'.

8.1.18.v: Up to (सामान्यवचनं) विभाषितं विशेषवचने (बहुवचनम्) [[8.1.74]], inclusive, should always be supplied the phrase 'the whole is unaccented, if it does not stand at the beginning of the foot of a verse'.

8.1.19.v: All the syllables of the Vocative Case are unaccented when a word precedes them and they do not stand at the beginning of a hemistich.

8.1.20.v: dual of युष्मद् and अस्मद् are substituted वाम and नौ respectively ।

8.1.21.v: For (the Genitive 6th-Case, Dative -4th Case and Accusative -2nd case) plural of युष्मद् and अस्मद् are substituted वस् and नस् respectively (when a word precedes and these substitutes are अनुदात्त).

8.1.22.v: For the Genitive 6th-Case and Dative -4th Case singular (of युष्मद् and अस्मद् are substituted) ते and मे respectively (when a word precedes and these substitutes are अनुदात्त).

8.1.23.v: For the Accusative -2nd case singular of युष्मद् and अस्मद् are substituted त्वा and मा respectively (when a word precedes and these substitutes are अनुदात्त).

8.1.24.v: when there is in connection with the सर्वनाम any of these - 1. च 'and' 2. वा 'or' 3. ह 'Oh!' 4. अह 'wonderful' or 5. एव 'only'.

8.1.25.v: The above substitutions do not take place also in connection with verbs having the sense of 'seeing' when physical seeing is not denoted.

8.1.26.v: When the सर्वनाम follows a Nominative 1st-Case, which itself is preceded by another word, then the above substitutions may take place optionally.

8.1.27.v: The words गोत्र etc. become unaccented after a finite verb when a contempt or a repetition in intended.

8.1.28.v: A finite verb is unaccented when a word precedes it which is not a finite verb.

8.1.29.v: By the लुट् (Periphrastic Future) is not unaccented when it is preceded by a word which is not a finite verb.

8.1.30.v: The finite verb retains its accent in connection with the particles 1. यत् 'that', 'because' 2. यदि 'if' 3. हन्त 'also', 'O!' 4. कुवित् 'well' 5. नेत् 'not' 6. चेत् 'if' 7. च 'if' 8. कच्चित् (interrogative particle implying 'I hope' or 'I hope not') and 9. यत्र 'where'.

8.1.31.v: The finite verb retains its accent in connection with नह when used in the sense of forbidding.

8.1.32.v: The finite verb retains its accent in connection with सत्य when used in asking a question.

8.1.33.v: The finite verb retains its accent in connection with अङ्ग when used in a friendly assertion.

8.1.34.v: The finite verb retains its accent in connection with हि when used in a friendly assertion.

8.1.35.v: In the छन्दस् (Vedas), the finite verb retains its accent (but not always) in connection with हि when it stands in correlation to another verb, even more than one.

8.1.36.v: The finite verb retains its accent in connection with यावत् and यथा।

8.1.37.v: But not so when these particles यावत् and यथा immediately precede the verb an denote 'praise'.

8.1.38.v: A finite verb loses its accent when it denotes 'praise' and is joined immediately with यावत् and यथा through the intervention of an उपसर्ग (verbal Preposition).

8.1.39.v: The finite verb retains its accent in connection with 1. तु 2. पश्य 3. पश्यत and 4. अह when meaning 'praise'.

8.1.40.v: The finite verb retains its accent in connection with अहो when meaning 'praise'.

8.1.41.v: The finite verb optionally retains its accent in connection with अहो in the remaining cases (i.e. where it does not mean 'praise').

8.1.42.v: The finite verb optionally retains its accent in connection with पुरा when it means 'haste' (i.e. when पुरा means 'before').

8.1.43.v: The finite verb optionally retains its accent in connection with ननु when with this particle, permission is asked.

8.1.44.v: The finite verb optionally retains its accent in connection with किम् when with this is asked a question relating to an action and when the verb is not preceded by a preposition or a negation.

8.1.45.v: When however किम् is not added in asking such a question, the finite verb may optionally retain its accent.

8.1.46.v: In connection with एहिमन्ये used diversely in the लृट् (I Future) that follows it, retains its accent.

8.1.47.v: The finite verb optionally retains its accent after जातु when this जातु is not preceded by another word.

8.1.48.v: Also after a form of किम् when the particle चित् follows it and when no other word precedes such form of किम् the finite verb retains its accent.

8.1.49.v: Also after an immediately preceding आहो and उताहो when these follow, no other word, the verb retains its accent.

8.1.50.v: When the above mentioned particles आहो and उताहो do not immediately precede the verb, the verb may optionally retain its accent.

8.1.51.v: The लृट् (I Future) retains its accent in connection with the Imperative of a verb denoting 'motion' ('to go', 'to come', 'to start' etc.) but only in that case, when the subject and object of both the verbs are not wholly different one from another.

8.1.52.v: Also an लोट् (Imperative Mood), following after an Imperative of verbs of 'motion' retains its accent when the subject or object of both the verbs is not wholly different.

8.1.53.v: An Imperative preceded by a preposition and not in the 1st person, following an Imperative of verbs of 'motion', may optionally retain its accent when the कारक is not wholly different.

8.1.54.v: An Imperative with a preposition preceding it, may optionally retain its accent, in connection with हन्त , but not in the 1st person.

8.1.55.v: After आम् , but separated from it by not more than one word, the Vocative retains its accent when the person addressed is not near.

8.1.56.v: A finite verb followed by यत् or हि or तु retains its accent in the छन्दस् (Vedas).

8.1.57.v: A finite verb retains its accent when it is not preceded by a गति Particle -- गतिश्च [[1.4.60]] etc., and when it is followed by 1. चन 2. चिद् 3. इव 4. गोत्र etc., a तद्धित affix, or by its own doubled form.

8.1.58.v: A finite verb, not preceded by a गति , retains its accent before the particles च (1. वा 2. ह 3. अह and 4. एव -- न चवाहाहैवयुक्ते [[8.1.24]]).

8.1.59.v: The first finite verb only retains its accent in connection with च and वा।

8.1.60.v: In connection with ह , the first finite verb retains its accent when an offence against custom is reprimanded.

8.1.61.v: In connection with अह , the first finite verb retains its accent when it refers to various commissions (as well as when a breach of good manners is condemned).

8.1.62.v: When च and अह are elided, the first finite verb still retains its accent when एव with the force of limitation, takes their place.

8.1.63.v: When च (1. वा 2. ह 3. अह and 4. एव -- न चवाहाहैवयुक्ते [[8.1.24]]) are elided the first verb optionally retains its accent.

8.1.64.v: Also in connection with वै and वाव , may optionally, in the छन्दस् (Vedas), the first verb retains its accent.

8.1.65.v: Also in connection with एक and अन्य , optionally in the छन्दस् (Vedas), the first verb retains its accent, when these word have the same meaning ('the one - the other').

8.1.66.v: In connection with यद् in all its forms, the verb retains its accent always.

8.1.67.v: After a word denoting praise belonging to काष्ठादि class the word whose praise is denoted, becomes अनुदात्त ।

8.1.68.v: (After such words denoting praise) the finite verb (which is praised) becomes अनुदात्त even along with the गति , if any, that may precede it.

8.1.69.v: A finite verb along with its preceding गति , if any, become अनुदात्त when a noun denoting the fault of the action follows, with the exception of गोत्र etc.

8.1.70.v: A गति becomes unaccented when followed by another गति .

8.1.71.v: A गति becomes अनुदात्त when followed by an accented finite verb.

8.1.72.v: A preceding Vocative is considered as non-existent (for the purposes of the accent of the following word and the enclitic forms of युष्मद् and अस्मद्).

8.1.73.v: A preceding Vocative, when it conveys a general idea, is not to be considered as if non-existent for the purposes of the subsequent Vocative, which stands in apposition with the former.

8.1.74.v: When the preceding Vocative is in the plural number, it is optionally considered as non-existent, if the subsequent Vocative, in apposition with it, is a specific term.
